citation.title: Improving Solar Cell Metallization Designs using Convolutional Neural Networks
citation.authors: Sumit Bhattacharya, Devanshu Arya, Debjani Bhowmick, Rajat Mani Thomas, Deepak Kumar Gupta
citation.venue: ICLR 2021 SimDL workshop paper; arXiv preprint (cs.CE)
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (8 Apr 2021; only version), full HTML text read from https://arxiv.org/html/2104.04017

included.reason: FT-DOMAIN (electrical conduction in solar-cell metallization; outside the §3.1 physics list)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (excluded: physics out of scope). Would-be primary outcome: on square cells with four busbar layouts, SolarNet designs reached higher efficiency than density-based TO, by up to 0.42 percentage points (3.5% relative); triangular cell 12.67% vs 12.31%.
claim.location: Section 4 Results, Figs. 2-3 (abstract, introduction and conclusion hold only qualitative comparisons)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not coded (excluded at full text); no runtime of either method is reported anywhere in the article.

notes: Excluded under PROTOCOL §3.1: the physics is electrical conduction in the front layer of a solar cell (Ohm's law with a nonlinear diode current source, Section 2; the objective is the cell's output power, Section 3). It is not elasticity, heat conduction or a compliant mechanism, and it is closest to the excluded electromagnetic class (§4). Judgment call for the verifier: if a scalar-conduction analogue of heat conduction is accepted, the record enters stratum Q (screening code was I-QUALITY) with the primary outcome above. Fig. 2 values: density-based TO 12.20, 12.05, 11.98, 12.55% vs SolarNet 12.34, 12.47, 12.25, 12.64% [pairing inferred from the stated maximum gain of 0.42 points, 3.5% relative]; Fig. 3 (triangle): 12.31% vs 12.67%. Would-be verdicts: R1 partial (R1-loose: same physics model and cell parameters (Table 1), TO density filter radius 1.5 elements, CNN output 200×200; TO optimizer, TO resolution, iteration counts and stopping rules not stated for either method; no budget comparison); R2 pass (unsure: TO settings largely unstated, nothing suggests a weak run); R3 na (per-problem CNN reparameterization with no offline training, no speed claim); R4 pass (unsure: efficiency of each returned design comes from the same FE model, and all five tested cases are shown; binarization of the CNN output is not stated). Informational reporting: 5 cases (4 busbar layouts on a 1.5 cm square cell, 1 triangular cell), one design shown per method and case, number of runs not stated; no seeds, timing or hardware; code link github.com/transmuteAI/SolarNet (footnote 1; repository not checked); no data statement.
